entries.ar: الصدق والكذب أصلهما في القول ماضيا كان أو مستقبلا وعدا كان أو غيره ، ولا يكونان بالقصد الأول إلا في القول ، ولا يكونان في القول إلا في الخبر دون غيره من أصناف الكلام ، ولذلك قال : **{ ومن أصدق من الله قيلا }** - **{ ومن أصدق من الله حديثا }** - **{ إنه كان صادق الوعد }** وقد يكونان بالعرض في غيره من أنواع الكلام كالاستفهام والأمر والدعاء ، وذلك نحو قول القائل أزيد في الدار فإن في ضمنه إخبارا بكونه جاهلا بحال زيد ، وكذا إذا قال واسني في ضمنه أنه محتاج إلى المواساة ، وإذا قال لا تؤذ ففي ضمنه أنه يؤذيه والصدق مطابقة القول الضمير والمخبر عنه مما ومتى انخرم شرط من ذلك لم يكن صدقا تاما بل إما أن لا يوصف بالصدق وإما أن يوصف تارة بالصدق وتارة بالكذب على نظرين مختلفين كقول كافر إذا قال من غير اعتقاد : محمد رسول الله ، فإن هذا يصح أن يقال صدق لكون المخبر عنه كذلك ، ويصح أن يقال كذب لمخالفة قوله ضميره ، وبالوجه الثاني إكذاب الله تعالى المنافقين حيث قالوا : **{ نشهد إنك لرسول الله }** الآية ، والصديق من كثر منه الصدق ، وقيل بل يقال لمن لا يكذب قط ، وقيل بل لمن لا يتأتى منه الكذب لتعوده الصدق ، وقيل بل لمن صدق بقوله واعتقاده وحقق صدقه بفعله ، قال : **{ واذكر في الكتاب إبراهيم إنه كان صديقا نبيا }** وقال **{ وأمه صديقة }** وقال **{ من النبيين والصديقين والشهداء }** فالصديقون هم قوم دوين الأنبياء في الفضيلة على ما بينت في الذريعة إلى مكارم الشريعة .
entries.en: Truthfulness (*al-ṣidq*) and falsehood (*al-kadhib*) have their origin in speech — whether of the past or the future, whether a promise or something else. By primary intent they belong only to speech, and within speech only to the declarative statement (*al-ḳabar*), not to the other classes of utterance. Hence He said: **{ And who is more truthful than God in speech? }** — **{ And who is more truthful than God in discourse? }** — **{ Indeed, he was true to his promise. }** They may, however, occur incidentally (*bi-l-ʿaraḋ*) in other kinds of utterance, such as the interrogative, the imperative, and the supplication. So when someone says “Is Zayd in the house?”, contained within it is a statement that the speaker is ignorant of Zayd's condition; likewise when he says “Assist me,” contained within it is that he stands in need of assistance; and when he says “Do not harm,” contained within it is that the other is harming him. Truthfulness is the correspondence of the utterance with the speaker's inner conviction and with the thing reported, together. Whenever one of these conditions is broken, it is not complete truthfulness; rather, either it is not described as truthful at all, or it is described as truthful in one respect and false in another. Take an unbeliever who says, without believing it, “Muḥammad is the Messenger of God.” It is sound to say he spoke truly, since the matter reported is indeed so; and sound to say he lied, since his utterance contradicts his inner conviction. It is in this second respect that God, exalted be He, pronounced the hypocrites liars when they said: **{ We bear witness that you are indeed the Messenger of God }** — the verse. *Al-ṣiddīq* is one from whom truthfulness issues abundantly. It is said: rather, it is applied to one who never lies at all. It is said: rather, to one from whom lying is not even possible, through his habituation to truthfulness. It is said: rather, to one who is truthful in his word and his belief and who realises his truthfulness in his deed. He said: **{ And mention in the Book Abraham; indeed he was a man of truth, a prophet }**, and He said **{ And his mother was a woman of truth }**, and He said **{ of the prophets, the truthful, and the witnesses }**. The *ṣiddīqūn* are a people ranking just below the prophets in excellence, as I have set out in *al-Dharīʿa ilā Makārim al-Sharīʿa*.
entries.note: The printed text reads مما where the sense requires معا (“together”); translated accordingly.

entries.ar: وقد يستعمل الصدق والكذب في كل ما يحق ويحصل في الإعتقاد نحو صدق ظني وكذب ، ويستعملان في أفعال الجوارح ، فيقال صدق في القتال إذا وفى حقه وفعل ما يجب وكما يجب ، وكذب في القتال إذا كان بخلاف ذلك ، قال : **{ رجال صدقوا ما عاهدوا الله عليه }** أي حققوا العهد بما أظهروه من أفعالهم ، وقوله : **{ ليسأل الصادقين عن صدقهم }** أي يسئل من صدق بلسانه عن صدق فعله تنبيها أنه لا يكفي الاعتراف بالحق دون تحريه بالفعل ، وقوله تعالى **{ لقد صدق الله رسوله الرؤيا بالحق }** فهذا صدق بالفعل وهو التحقق أي حقق رؤيته ، وعلى ذلك قوله : **{ والذي جاء بالصدق وصدق به }** أي حقق ما أورده قولا بما تحراه فعلا ويعبر عن كل فعل فاضل ظاهرا وباطنا بالصدق فيضاف إليه ذلك الفعل الذي يوصف به نحو قوله : **{ في مقعد صدق عند مليك مقتدر }** وعلى هذا **{ أن لهم قدم صدق عند ربهم }** وقوله **{ أدخلني مدخل صدق وأخرجني مخرج صدق }** - **{ واجعل لي لسان صدق في الآخرين }** فإن ذلك سؤال أن يجعله الله تعالى صالحا بحيث إذا أثنى عليه من بعده لم يكن ذلك الثناء كذبا بل يكون كما قال الشاعر : ( إذا نحن أثنينا عليك بصالح % % فأنت الذي نثني وفوق الذي نثنى ) وصدق قد يتعدى إلى مفعولين نحو **{ ولقد صدقكم الله وعده }** وصدقت فلانا نسبته إلى الصدق وأصدقته وجدته صادقا ، وقيل هما واحد ويقالان فيهما جميعا قال **{ ولما جاءهم رسول من عند الله مصدق لما معهم }** - **{ وقفينا على آثارهم بعيسى ابن مريم مصدقا لما بين يديه }** ويستعمل التصديق في كل ما فيه تحقيق ، يقال صدقني فعله وكتابه ، قال **{ ولما جاءهم كتاب من عند الله مصدق لما معهم }** - **{ نزل عليك الكتاب بالحق مصدقا لما بين يديه }** - **{ وهذا كتاب مصدق لسانا عربيا }** أي مصدق ما تقدم وقوله : لسانا منتصب على الحال وفي المثل : صدقني سن بكره .
entries.en: *Al-ṣidq* and *al-kadhib* are also used of whatever proves true and is settled in belief, as in “my supposition proved true” or “proved false.” They are used, too, of the acts of the limbs: one says he was true in battle when he discharged its due and did what must be done as it must be done, and he was false in battle when it was otherwise. He said: **{ Men who were true to the covenant they made with God }** — that is, they realised the covenant by what they made manifest in their deeds. And His words **{ That He may question the truthful about their truthfulness }** — that is, He questions the one truthful with his tongue about the truthfulness of his deed, alerting us that acknowledging the truth does not suffice without pursuing it in action. And His words, exalted be He, **{ God has certainly fulfilled His Messenger's vision in truth }** — this is truthfulness by deed, namely realisation; that is, He made his vision come true. Of the same kind are His words **{ And he who brought the truth and confirmed it }** — that is, he realised in deed what he had put forward in word. Every excellent act, outward and inward, is expressed by *ṣidq*, and the act so described is annexed to it, as in His words **{ In a seat of truth with a Sovereign Omnipotent }**, and likewise **{ That they have a sure footing with their Lord }**, and His words **{ Cause me to enter by an entrance of truth and bring me out by an exit of truth }** — **{ And grant me a tongue of truth among those who come after }**. For that is a petition that God, exalted be He, make him righteous, such that if one who comes after him praises him, that praise would be no lie; rather it would be as the poet said: *When we praise you for some good, you are the very thing we praise — and beyond what we praise.* *Ṣaddaqa* may govern two objects, as in **{ God had certainly fulfilled to you His promise }**. *Ṣaddaqtu fulānan* — I ascribed truthfulness to him; *aṣdaqtuhu* — I found him truthful. It is said the two are one and are used in both senses alike. He said **{ And when a messenger came to them from God, confirming what was with them }** — **{ And We caused Jesus son of Mary to follow in their footsteps, confirming what was before him }**. *Al-taṣdīq* is used of everything in which there is verification: one says “his deed confirmed me,” and “his writing confirmed me.” He said **{ And when a Book came to them from God, confirming what was with them }** — **{ He has sent down upon you the Book with the truth, confirming what was before it }** — **{ And this is a Book confirming, in the Arabic tongue }** — that is, confirming what came before; and His word *lisānan* stands in the accusative as a circumstantial qualifier (*ḥāl*). And in the proverb: *ṣadaqanī sinna bakrihi* — “he told me the truth about the age of his young camel.”
entries.note: The % marks in the verse indicate the hemistich division of the printed edition.

entries.ar: والصداقة صدق الإعتقاد في المودة وذلك مختص بالإنسان دون غيره قال **{ فما لنا من شافعين ولا صديق حميم }** وذلك إشارة إلى نحو قوله **{ الأخلاء يومئذ بعضهم لبعض عدو إلا المتقين }** ، والصدقة ما يخرجه الإنسان من ماله على وجه القربة كالزكاة لكن الصدقة في الأصل تقال للمتطوع به والزكاة للواجب ، وقد يسمى الواجب صدقة إذا تحرى صاحبها الصدق في فعله قال **{ خذ من أموالهم صدقة }** وقال **{ إنما الصدقات للفقراء }** يقال صدق وتصدق قال **{ فلا صدق ولا صلى }** - **{ إن الله يجزي المتصدقين }** - **{ إن المصدقين والمصدقات }** في آي كثيرة .
entries.en: *Al-ṣadāqa* — friendship — is truthfulness of conviction in affection, and this belongs to man and to no other. He said **{ So we have no intercessors, nor any devoted friend }**, which alludes to the like of His words **{ Close friends, on that Day, will be enemies to one another — except the God-fearing }**. *Al-ṣadaqa* is what a person gives out of his wealth by way of drawing near to God, like *al-zakāt*; but *ṣadaqa* is properly said of what is given voluntarily, and *zakāt* of what is obligatory. The obligatory may yet be called *ṣadaqa* when the giver pursues truthfulness in his act. He said **{ Take alms from their wealth }**, and He said **{ Alms are only for the poor }**. One says *ṣaddaqa* and *taṣaddaqa*. He said **{ He neither gave alms nor prayed }** — **{ Indeed God rewards those who give alms }** — **{ Indeed the almsgiving men and the almsgiving women }**, in many verses.

entries.ar: ويقال لما تجافى عنه الإنسان من حقه تصدق به نحو قوله **{ والجروح قصاص فمن تصدق به فهو كفارة له }** أي من تجافى عنه ، وقوله **{ وإن كان ذو عسرة فنظرة إلى ميسرة وأن تصدقوا خير لكم }** فإنه أجرى ما يسامح به المعسر مجرى الصدقة وعلى هذا ما ورد عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم ما تأكله العافية فهو صدقة وعلى هذا قوله **{ فدية مسلمة إلى أهله }** **{ إلا أن يصدقوا }** فسمي إعفاءه صدقة ، وقوله **{ فقدموا بين يدي نجواكم صدقة }** أأشفقتم أن تقدموا بين يدى نجواكم صدقات فإنهم كانوا قد أمروا بأن يتصدق من يناجي الرسول بصدقة ما غير مقدرة .
entries.en: Of what a person relinquishes of his own right it is said that he “gave it as alms,” as in His words **{ And for wounds, retaliation; but whoever gives it away as charity, it is an expiation for him }** — that is, whoever relinquishes it. And His words **{ And if the debtor is in hardship, then respite until ease; and that you remit it as charity is better for you }** — for He made what is forgiven the man in hardship run the course of alms. On this basis is what has come down from the Prophet, God bless him and grant him peace: *what the foraging creatures eat of it is alms.* And likewise His words **{ and a blood-payment delivered to his family }** **{ unless they remit it as charity }** — so his waiving of it is named *ṣadaqa*. And His words **{ Then offer alms before your private consultation }**, **{ Have you been afraid to offer alms before your private consultation? }** — for they had been commanded that whoever consults the Messenger privately should give some alms, of no fixed amount.
entries.note: أأشفقتم أن تقدموا بين يدي نجواكم صدقات is Q. 58:13, unmarked as a quotation in the printed text; marked here.

entries.ar: وقوله **{ رب لولا أخرتني إلى أجل قريب فأصدق وأكن من الصالحين }** فمن الصدق أو من الصدقة . وصداق المرأة وصداقها وصدقتها ما تعطى من مهرها ، وقد أصدقتها ، قال **{ وآتوا النساء صدقاتهن نحلة }** .
entries.en: And His words **{ My Lord, if only You would grant me respite for a brief term, so that I might give alms and be among the righteous }** — this is either from *al-ṣidq* or from *al-ṣadaqa*. And *ṣidāq* of a woman, and *ṣadāquhā*, and *ṣaduqatuhā*: what she is given of her dower; and *aṣdaqtuhā* — I assigned her a dower. He said **{ And give women their dowers as a free gift }**.
